1.explanation:
• DataTable/DataTable.mdx: shows the API for TableExpandHeader and TableExpandRow, where id generation should occur.
• DataTable/docs/overview.mdx: contains example markup and guidance on header and row props, illustrating where IDs are expected.
• DataTable/stories/expansion: the exact Storybook example where the violation is reproduced (the “DataTable with expansion” story).
• DataTable/state: contains the internal stateful example logic that wires getRowProps/getHeaderProps, which carries header IDs into the rendered cells.
• DataTable/tools: includes utility functions that may generate or assign unique IDs for table headers and rows.
• DataTable/migrate-to-7.x.md: documents any breaking changes around prop names or ID handling when migrating, useful to see if ID behavior changed in v7.
1.bug_scenario: In the expansion example of the DataTable, the first column is rendered via <TableExpandHeader> (in the header row) and each row renders a corresponding expansion cell via <TableExpandRow> which outputs <td headers="expand"…>. The IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker flags these cells because the “headers” attribute value “expand” does not reference any valid id in the document — in other words, the <th> generated by <TableExpandHeader> isn’t being given a matching id. Without that id on the header cell, the <td headers="expand"> references break, leading to an accessibility violation.
